page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, providing a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across several standard operations, alongside some notable limitations. The instance achieves average scores in memory bandwidth read-only tests, reaching 414.69 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 39.89 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform within average ranges. However, multi-core CPU performance and write bandwidth for large memory blocks fall into the lower 25% tier. Cryptographic operations, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression benchmarks also show weaker performance.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.cm4.2xlarge is qualitatively positioned as a legacy general-purpose resource. It is suitable for workloads that require steady CPU allocation without extreme compute or memory demands, such as static web serving, basic text processing, and lightweight Redis caching. It is not recommended for intensive database operations, heavy multi-threaded processing, or medium-to-large language model inference due to poor benchmark results in those areas.
